content: No better burden can a traveler carry than a store of common sense; no worse provision can he take across the field than excessive drinking.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: Byrði betri berr-at maðr brautu at (Hávamál, Stanzas 10 & 12) — Poetic Edda
explanation: Out on the unforgiving trails and across icy waters, material wealth is heavy and easily stolen, but a clear, sound mind weighs nothing and preserves your life at every turn. Conversely, indulging in excessive drink dulls judgment, strips away honor, and leaves a traveler defenseless in hostile territory.
practicalInsight: Protect your mental clarity today. Choose keen awareness and self-restraint over numbing distractions or intoxicants.
reflectionPrompt: What burden are you currently carrying through life that clouds your mind rather than sharpening your perception?
